meta.title: Changelog — Aethyr
meta.description: Version history and release notes for the Aethyr MCP server for Unreal Engine 5.

article.heading: Changelog
article.lead: What's new in the Aethyr MCP server for Unreal Engine 5.

sections.heading: 0.6.10, October 2026
sections.html:
rollback_update works while the server is running. Windows refused to overwrite the running exe, so every rollback failed with error 5. It now renames the running exe aside, puts the restored exe in its name, and returns restart_required. The restored exe runs from the next client start, so restart your AI client afterwards.

The first health_check after an update no longer reports a daemon start that the update cut off as a launch failure. A start whose process has exited reads as interrupted, and doctor lists it as a warning. A failure from a process that is still running, or one with a known cause, still reads as a failure.

Upgrading: a 0.6.8 install or later can use apply_update as usual. A precompiled install from 0.6.7 or earlier should update with setup this once, by following install.md, not with apply_update. A source install can use apply_update as usual.

Downloads and the full notes, including known issues, are on the download page.

sections.heading: 0.6.9, October 2026
sections.html:
get_class_info now says where a class is declared, with include_path, module_relative_path and module. Function rows add is_deprecated, deprecation_message and a defaults object. get_active_cook_target reports installed_platforms, the exact values set_active_cook_target, cook_content and package_project accept. list_metasound_node_classes takes include_all. Results from commandlet ops carry served_by, and a fall back to a one-shot editor adds a warning. set_config_value replies with persisted and disk_path.

health_check lists a plugin the .uproject enables but that is on disk nowhere in plugin_warnings, since the editor may crash on launch. The editor has aethyr.live_server.start and aethyr.live_server.stop console commands, and warns when another process holds Epic's MCP port. The Aethyr Project Settings now do something: bAutoStartLiveServer and LiveServerPort drive the live server, and Emit Tool Meta or AETHYR_EMIT_TOOL_META turn the _meta block on tool results off.

set_config_value now writes where the value survives a restart, reads the file back before it says ok, and names the file when a write can't land. delete_asset refuses on soft referencers too unless force is true. bp_structural_diff returns {ok, identical, differences}, so a diff that finds differences no longer reads ok:false. apply_ops fails fast when the daemon can't start, and a failed atomic batch discards the assets it created.

Fixes: a // or /.. in an Epic bridge or editor-state argument is a tool error before it can crash the editor. set_niagara_module_input with mode=linked no longer crashes on an enum input it can't resolve. set_material_parameter and set_material_instance_parameter refuse bad input instead of applying a zero. read_material reports the real input name in to_pin. compile_function wires {var} correctly. Property writes report the real value for a false bool or zero. The HTTP daemon no longer leaks memory, and a call to a wedged editor ends at its timeout.

Upgrading: a 0.6.8 install can use apply_update as usual. A precompiled install from 0.6.7 or earlier should update with setup this once, by following install.md, not with apply_update. A source install can use apply_update as usual.

Downloads and the full notes, including known issues, are on the download page.

sections.heading: 0.6.8, October 2026
sections.html:
Setup now checks your engine before it writes anything. The precompiled zip only fits a stock UE 5.8, and the editor refuses modules built for another engine build. On a custom or source-built engine, setup says so and steers to the source zip. --flavor precompiled on a mismatch is refused with buildid_mismatch, and the comparison shows up as build_id_check. Setup also warns when the engine is older than 5.8.

The build_editor step names the whole editor target, which builds both modules and writes the manifest. doctor reports a manifest that is missing or lists only one of them. A failed Perforce write names the file and tells you what to do about one another workspace has opened.

A client opened above your project folder now finds the project. With no .uproject in or above the working directory, the one project below it with Aethyr installed is used and reported as project_source: cwd_child. health_check splits current from history, so a daemon start that later recovered no longer looks like a live problem.

Setup keeps a skill or agent you changed and reports it as user_modified from the second run after upgrading, since the first run records the hashes. The audit agent is read-only on Copilot CLI and Gemini CLI now, the way it already was on Claude Code.

Fixes: list_subobjects with include_properties no longer crashes on a Widget Blueprint that has a Button. Bad paths such as /Game//X.X in tool arguments are refused before they can crash the editor. The update helper should now find a running hub. apply_update keeps a precompiled install precompiled, and a write that fails partway, such as on a full disk, no longer leaves a plugin file truncated or an editor DLL missing.

Upgrading a precompiled install from 0.6.7 or earlier: update with setup this once, by following install.md, not with apply_update. The older updater reads a precompiled install as a source install and would remove its prebuilt DLLs. 0.6.8 fixes that for later updates, and setup puts the precompiled plugin back if an update already went wrong. Your instruction files stop gaining blank lines on a repeat run.

Downloads and the full notes, including known issues, are on the download page.

sections.heading: 0.6.7, October 2026
sections.html:
Aethyr's skills now install for whichever AI client you use. Setup puts the aethyr-* skills in ~/.agents/skills, which Copilot CLI, VS Code, Codex, Gemini CLI, Cursor and Windsurf read, and in ~/.claude/skills for Claude Code. The read-only audit agent, now called aethyr-bp-audit, goes to Claude Code, Copilot CLI and Gemini CLI in each one's own format.

Your assistant asks once whether to install the skills. Only an explicit no skips them. --no-skills now skips just the skills and the agent, and the new --no-guidance skips the short section in your clients' instruction files. The dry run lists everything the real run will do, including removing an old agent copy.

The aethyr-core skill also loads in Copilot CLI now. Its description wasn't valid YAML, so strict loaders skipped it.

Downloads and the full notes, including known issues, are on the download page.

sections.heading: 0.6.6, October 2026
sections.html:
Aethyr now comes with sample content you can build into your project in one request. Ask your assistant to "install the Aethyr samples" and the new install_samples tool builds 17 small assets into /Game/AethyrSamples: an enemy, a boss, a turret, a pickup, a door, a crate, a loot table with its struct and rarity enum, rock and lava materials, a main menu, a HUD, and an enemy blackboard and behavior tree. A few carry a bug on purpose, so the tutorials have something to fix. Nothing ships as a .uasset. Re-running skips what already exists and never overwrites your own assets.

Six new tools create data tables, enums, widget blueprints, blackboards, blackboard keys and behavior trees, all without a running editor. Material parameters can be named when you add them. A path like /Game//Enemy no longer crashes the editor.

This release also includes everything planned for 0.6.5, which wasn't published on its own. Aethyr steps aside while you compile your project. Its headless editor no longer breaks a build with LNK1104. It picks your editor build configuration, Development or DebugGame, by itself. And both downloads now carry the same plugin, apart from the compiled modules.

Downloads and the full notes, including known issues, are on the download page.

sections.heading: 0.6.3, October 2026
sections.html:
Aethyr is free to use, for anything. The end user license agreement is gone, and Aethyr now ships under the Aethyr License. You can use it, change it, and ship it, commercial games and tools included. The one condition is giving credit to Doug Fessler in what you ship, for example "Aethyr by Doug Fessler (https://aethyr.gg)" in your credits, an About screen, your docs, or a README. The licensing page explains it, and every download carries the full text as LICENSE.md.

Downloads and the full notes are on the download page.

sections.heading: 0.6.2, October 2026
sections.html:
Setup now leaves your project alone. Asking your assistant to "get Aethyr from aethyr.gg" installs Aethyr, gives it full read and write access, and turns on Epic's MCP bridge, while writing only to Aethyr's own folder, the project's Saved folder, Config/DefaultAethyr.ini only if you pass --deny, and config files in your user profile. Your .uproject, config files, AGENTS.md and other project files aren't touched.

Epic's MCP plugin now comes in through Aethyr's own plugin file, editor only, and Aethyr starts Epic's server for you. One MCP entry serves whichever project your AI client is opened in, and AethyrMcp.exe launch-editor can start the editor with the bridge on for a single session.

Downloads and the full notes, including known issues, are on the download page.

sections.heading: 0.6.1, October 2026
sections.html:
A small follow-up to 0.6.0. If an editor was still open when an update finished, its new editor DLLs could stay staged for good. Now the next setup, a confirmed apply_update, or a server start finishes the swap once nothing holds them and they match the release, and doctor and health_check tell you while any are waiting. setup --dry-run also now says "would add" for MCP client configs instead of reading as if it had written them.

Downloads and the full notes are on the download page.

sections.heading: 0.6.0, October 2026
sections.html:
Tell your AI assistant "get Aethyr from aethyr.gg" or "update Aethyr" and it can now do the whole job. The new install page walks an assistant through it, and the AethyrMcp.exe setup command does the work in one run. It picks and verifies the right zip for your engine, stops only your project's Aethyr servers, and replaces the plugin folder cleanly. It also installs the skills, registers Aethyr with your MCP clients, sets up Epic's MCP bridge, and finishes with a health check. Use --dry-run to see the plan first.

apply_update now removes files a release dropped, updates the precompiled editor DLLs, and works in projects inside a git repository. A plugin denylist can live in Config/DefaultAethyr.ini, list replies stay under about 16 KB with an honest cursor, and doctor no longer raises false errors for platform-folder plugins.

Downloads and the full notes, including known issues, are on the download page.

sections.heading: 0.5.2, September 2026
sections.html:
A field-report release. With two engines installed, Aethyr could launch the wrong one and fail every headless tool call because a project plugin was built for the other engine. Aethyr now checks the engine against the one your project was built with. It sets aside a stale project plugin instead of failing the launch, and it tells you which engine to use when the better match is a different engine version. Updating the plugin now clears its old generated headers, which fixes the GENERATED_BODY "missing type specifier" build error after an update.

health_check now says in one sentence whether you have a healthy live editor or a headless editor that can't start, and why. It reports the live editor and the headless daemon separately, and names the engine Aethyr launches.

list_assets can return a whole folder tree as one readable inventory. It groups by folder or class, includes redirectors, flags broken redirectors, redirector chains, and duplicate names, and can export the full list to CSV, JSON, or Markdown.

Downloads and the full notes, including known issues, are on the download page.

sections.heading: 0.5.1, September 2026
sections.html:
The Fab build now allows writes by default and carries every tool, the same as the full build. A bridged Epic write follows the same read-only rule as any other write. A live editor no longer crashes when close_asset_editor closes a Widget Blueprint editor, move_asset works on Blueprints with breakpoints, delete_asset finds referencers in every project mount, and the bridge follows a changed Epic MCP port.

Fab installs still update through Fab. While Aethyr is working, the editor keeps running at full speed even in the background, and it goes back to normal a few seconds after the last request.

Downloads and the full notes, including known issues, are on the download page.

sections.heading: 0.5.0, September 2026
sections.html:
Aethyr now bridges to Unreal's own tools. The Engine Toolset Bridge talks to Epic's ModelContextProtocol server inside a running UE 5.8 editor, so your assistant can reach Epic's toolsets (Niagara, Sequencer, GAS, UMG, Slate UI, play-in-editor, and more) through Aethyr. It's on by default in every build, including Fab. Turn on Epic's ModelContextProtocol plugin and the toolsets you want in your project, then use epic_list_toolsets, epic_describe_toolset, and epic_call_tool.

Every Epic tool is sorted into reads and writes, and anything unclear counts as a write. The Fab build stays read-only (0.5.1 changed this). It refuses bridged writes until you turn writes on, and it backs up the target asset before any bridged write.

28 tools that needed a live editor anyway, and that Unreal now does just as well, are removed. Calling one tells your assistant which Epic tool replaces it and which plugin to enable. Tools that work without an editor open all stay. Aethyr now needs UE 5.8 or later.

Downloads and the full notes, including the migration table and known issues, are on the download page.

sections.heading: 0.4.2, September 2026
sections.html:
Every MCP client on a project now shares one Aethyr server instead of starting its own. Aethyr also finds your engine without relying on the .uproject's per-machine engine ID, so a custom or source-built engine works on a fresh machine.

Aethyr can now update itself: health_check and a notice at connect tell your assistant when a new release is out, and apply_update installs it once you say yes, with an automatic rollback if the new version fails its check. Setup got easier too: a plugin your machine doesn't have no longer stops the headless editor, a failed headless start is reported instead of showing empty results, and doctor checks that your MCP client has Aethyr registered.

Downloads and the full notes, including known issues, are on the download page.

sections.heading: 0.4.1, September 2026
sections.html:
A patch release. Six tools that could crash the headless editor when no editor was open, get_landscape_paint_state, get_foliage_paint_state, get_mesh_paint_state, get_texture_paint_state, get_modeling_state, and focus_actor, now answer that they need a running editor instead. The selection tools say the same. reset_project_setting no longer wipes your per-user settings file.

Downloads and the full notes, including known issues, are on the download page.

sections.heading: 0.4.0, September 2026
sections.html:
Every tool now has a functional test that drives it against a real editor and checks the result with a separate read. That pass found and fixed more than twenty tools that reported the wrong result or did less than they said, among them move_asset on the headless editor, bind_widget_event, set_component_property with a false bool, and the DataTable tools on Blueprint structs.

The 25 editor-state tools that used to answer valid:false now read real state: the outliner, the details panel, the paint and modeling modes, Take Recorder, the Movie Render Queue, changelists, cook progress, DDC usage, and more. set_active_cook_target and reset_project_setting are new, and health_check no longer reports "auth rejected" when two editors start on one machine.

Downloads and the full notes, including known issues, are on the download page.

sections.heading: 0.3.0, September 2026
sections.html:
Aethyr can now read custom graph assets, not just Blueprints. get_graph and the new list_graphs read any asset that owns editor graphs, and the new list_subobjects shows how a custom graph's nodes reference each other. read_actor_instance reads a nested object by its full object path instead of returning the parent asset.

You can compare an asset against an older source-control revision. get_asset_history lists its revisions through Unreal's own provider, so Perforce, Git, and Plastic all work. load_asset_revision loads one for the normal read tools, and unload_packages cleans up afterward.

A plugin that breaks the headless editor now gets quarantined automatically, and AETHYR_PLUGIN_DENYLIST finally takes effect. run_python_script and the four ui_* tools are on by default. Set AETHYR_ALLOW_PYTHON=0 or AETHYR_ALLOW_UI=0 to turn one off. health_check also recovers after an editor restart instead of reporting it unreachable.

Downloads and the full notes, including known issues, are on the download page.

sections.heading: 0.2.0, September 2026
sections.html:
Write tools report whether the write landed, implement_interface no longer takes down the headless editor on a bare interface name, and free-text arguments keep their double quotes. The server finds a Launcher-installed engine on its own, so AETHYR_ENGINE_DIR is no longer required for a stock install.

Downloads and the full notes, including known issues, are on the download page.

sections.heading: 0.1.1, September 2026
sections.html:
The two material Set tools now report the backend's real result. set_material_parameter and set_material_instance_parameter used to answer ok:true even when the write failed, for example on an unknown parameter or a value that wouldn't parse.

Downloads and the full notes, including known issues, are on the download page.

sections.heading: 0.1.0, September 2026
sections.html:
The first public release. Version numbering restarted at 0.1.0 on 2026-07-08, and the standalone desktop app that used to accompany releases was removed. The plugin, the server, and the scripts are the product.

It was published after 0.1.1, which supersedes it with a fix for a false success on the two material Set tools. Take the newest release unless you have a reason to pin this one.

Downloads and the full notes, including known issues, are on the download page.
